correctness.rationale: The original concerns the ordinary unweighted bipartite graph of complex geometric nodes and Jacobi planes. To check the node list, on the hyperplane σ1=0, Newton's identity gives σ4=p2²/8−p4/4, where pj is the j-th power sum. At a singular point all x_i satisfy the same cubic x_i³−(p2/2)x_i=constant. Two distinct values of multiplicities m and 6−m would require m(6−m)=6, which is impossible, and one value gives the zero vector. For three distinct values a,b,c one has a+b+c=0 and Σ(m_i−1)a_i²=0. The partitions (4,1,1), (3,2,1), (2,2,2) give respectively the two-support nodes, no solution, and the three-colour nodes. In both admissible cases the restricted quartic Hessian has only the radial kernel on the hyperplane: solve (3x_i²−p2/2)v_i−x_i(x·v)=c with Σv_i=0. The forty classical Jacobi planes have the stated equations; the product of the three factors on the selected coordinates is 1+u³z³ in the elementary-symmetric generating polynomial, so σ4=0 on each plane. I rebuilt every incidence by exact arithmetic in Z[ω], with no reduction to characteristic seven. Degrees 8 and 9, 360 incidences, and direct integral Smith and determinant computations with FLINT on two 84-by-84 cofactors give 1^40,2^14,4,12^6,60^3,120^5,360,720^4,2160^10 and determinant 2^108 * 3^54 * 5^23, confirming connectedness and exponent 2160. The submitted reference to an embedding into F7 is shorthand for specialization of Eisenstein integers, not a field embedding of Q(ω); the direct characteristic-zero incidence proof makes this immaterial.

value.rationale: The complete bipartite incidence joins two intrinsic families on a classical singular quartic. Its graph Jacobian measures integral chip-firing equivalence and supplies the exact primary and exponent data needed to study divisor classes on this finite graph. The simultaneous 2-, 3-, and 5-primary structure and 44 nonunit factors go beyond the earlier rectangular defect and are not determined by spanning-tree order. This is useful as exact reference data, not a claim about geometric class groups.
residual_risks: Single finite configuration; no general incidence theorem, moduli application, or equivariant critical-group classification is claimed.
